blocks.title: You'll want to know: mūniceps, mūnicipis

segments.text: mūniceps, mūnicipis — "a citizen of a free town; a fellow townsman".
Ille mūniceps meus est. He comes from my home town.
mūniceps, mūnicipis m. and f.: one who took on the duties of a self-governing Italian town.
mūniceps is built from mūnus "a duty, a service" and capiō "to take" (EtymDB; Lewis & Short): one who takes on the town's duties.
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.

blocks.title: You'll want to know: decuriō, decuriōnis

segments.text: decuriō, decuriōnis — "a town councillor; a cavalry officer".
Decuriōnēs dē aquaeductū dēlīberāvērunt. The town councillors deliberated about the aqueduct.
decuriō, decuriōnis m. In a town the decuriōnēs formed the council; in the army a decuriō led ten horsemen. Built on decem, ten.
decuriō is built on decuria "a group of ten" (EtymDB; Lewis & Short), which comes from decem "ten".

blocks.title: You'll want to know: colōnia, colōniae

segments.text: colōnia, colōniae — "a colony, a settlement".
Mīlitēs in colōniam missī sunt. Soldiers were sent to the settlement.
colōnia, colōniae f., built on colōnus, a settler, a farmer. Many cities of Europe began as Roman colonies. English colony.
colōnia is built on colōnus "a settler, a farmer" (EtymDB), which comes from colō "to till, to dwell" (Lewis & Short). English colony comes from it.

blocks.title: You'll want to know: sodālis, sodālis

segments.text: sodālis, sodālis — "a companion, a comrade; a club member".
Cum sodālibus cēnāvit. He dined with his comrades.
sodālis, sodālis m. and f. Members of a club, a guild or a priestly brotherhood were sodālēs.
The origin of sodālis is not settled: Lewis & Short compare it with a root meaning "one's own way, custom", but give no sure account.

blocks.title: You'll want to know: collēgium, collēgiī

segments.text: collēgium, collēgiī — "an association, a guild; a board of officials".
Fabrī in collēgium convēnērunt. The craftsmen met in their guild.
collēgium, collēgiī n., built on collēga, a colleague. Guilds of craftsmen and boards of priests were both collēgia. English college.
collēgium is built on collēga "a colleague, one chosen with another" (EtymDB; Lewis & Short). English college comes from it.

segments.text: An advocate? (causidicus, causidicī.) A client? (cliēns, clientis.) A shipowner? (nāviculārius, nāviculāriī.) A copyist? (librārius, librāriī.) A land surveyor? (agrīmēnsor, agrīmēnsōris.) A senator? (senātor, senātōris.) Patrician? (patricius, patricia, patricium.) Plebeian? (plēbēius, plēbēia, plēbēium.) Well known? (nōbilis, nōbile.) Of the people? (populāris, populāre.) A public office? (magistrātus, magistrātūs.) A praetor? (praetor, praetōris.) An aedile? (aedīlis, aedīlis.) A quaestor? (quaestor, quaestōris.) A censor? (cēnsor, cēnsōris.) A vote? (suffrāgium, suffrāgiī.) The voting assembly? (comitia, comitiōrum.) A candidate? (candidātus, candidātī.) Canvassing? (ambitiō, ambitiōnis.) To pick out? (ēligō, ēligere.) To rule? (regō, regere.) To steer? (gubernō, gubernāre.) To manage? (administrō, administrāre.) Command? (imperium, imperiī.) The first? (prīnceps, prīncipis.) A partnership? (societās, societātis.) Human nature? (hūmānitās, hūmānitātis.) A custom? (mōs, mōris.) An institution? (īnstitūtum, īnstitūtī.) Harmony? (concordia, concordiae.) Disagreement? (discordia, discordiae.) A rising? (sēditiō, sēditiōnis.) Seditious? (sēditiōsus, sēditiōsa, sēditiōsum.) Stormy? (turbulentus, turbulenta, turbulentum.) To stir up? (concitō, concitāre.) A citizen of a free town? (mūniceps, mūnicipis.) A town councillor? (decuriō, decuriōnis.) A colony? (colōnia, colōniae.) A companion? (sodālis, sodālis.) An association? (collēgium, collēgiī.)
